items.title: The objects killed by the localization functor at a multiplicative system
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file homology.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma characterizes the objects that the localization functor at a multiplicative system sends to zero, by the existence of a zero morphism into or out of the object that belongs to the multiplicative system (statement lines 2101-2113). The proof is a complete argument: two of the implications follow because the localized image of an element of the system is an isomorphism and an additive category has no nontrivial isomorphism on a zero object (proof lines 2116-2118); the remaining ones use the criterion describing which morphisms become invertible to produce an element of the system from the vanishing of the localized object (proof lines 2119-2124 and 2125). The non-formal content is the application of the inversion criterion. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
